items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Around them Mommaloos in that area? [INTERVIEWEE] That's right.

ctx.x: Well, they'd just make you blow your heart out, Dick, that's all. I've seen myself blow so much, split my lip wide open. Just trying to hit them high notes at them, you know. And that's what the whole thing was. They'd just see who could out blow the other fella. And man, that music in those tin roof camps really sound nice. Incidentally, I played a job about five years ago on the 4th of July with Johnny McGee. He played with me and old Bill Wally was with us. We had a five piece combo. Talk about sounding nice,…
Around them Mommaloos in that area?

That's right. And we had Bill on bass, myself on trumpet, Johnny McGee playing clarinet, Tony Shrine on drums, and Sam Callie on guitar. You ever hear him play guitar? I think a long time ago with you. Oh man, he sounds like a piano man on a guitar. You don't need a piano, Paul, when you play with him. Really nice. He still plays nice.
